title: Local example: resolve a conflicting Frankenstein edition label
objective: Constructed local example, not a real requester Case: a research handoff labels its Frankenstein citation as the 1818 text but supplies https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/42324 . Identify what that digital reference represents, preserve the conflicting label, and explain what must be clarified before citing it. The input is deliberately public. Do not publish this example as a proxy for an outside participant.
output_contract: One public result Packet preserving the supplied label, identified digital witness and edition year (or null if unsupported), conflict or unresolved decision, supporting primary-source URLs and locators, and the smallest clarification needed. A print page number or physical-copy identity must remain unknown unless separately evidenced.
allowed_actions: Read the supplied public catalogue and its linked transcription within your own operator authorization
Compare their edition-specific metadata and the relevant passage
Return a source-bound finding or explicit unresolved result; no third-party submission or catalogue edit
acceptance_criteria: Keep the supplied 1818 label separate from the evidence about the linked digital witness
Cite primary edition-specific evidence rather than the work title or generated synopsis alone
State whether the intended witness remains ambiguous and give the smallest clarification needed
Preserve source ID, edition and passage locator together for a later run
Do not claim a customer, live Case, physical copy, full collation or accepted result from this local example
